title: The pullback of a finite type module is of finite type
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], i.e. every point of $Y$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G|_V$ for some $n\ge0$. Then the pullback $f^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type: every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow(f^*\mathcal G)|_U$ (one may take $U=f^{-1}V$ and the same $n$ as for $\mathcal G$ on $V$).

source.place: Sheaves of Modules (modules.tex), Lemma 01B6 (lemma-pullback-finite-type), stated there for a morphism of ringed spaces; its proof uses that $f^*$ is right exact and commutes with direct sums (Lemma 01AJ, lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback), $f^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X$, and that pullback commutes with restriction to opens (argument of Lemma 01B3, lemma-pullback-locally-generated)

proof.text: *Step 1 (set-up and reduction to $V$).* Let $x\in X$ and $y=f(x)$. Since $\mathcal G$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] there are an open $V\ni y$, an $n\ge0$ and a surjection $\varphi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_V$ of $\mathcal O_V$-modules. Put $U=f^{-1}V$, an open neighbourhood of $x$, regard $V$ and $U$ as open subschemes [def-pc-scheme] with inclusions $j:V\to Y$, $j':U\to X$, which are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $f':U\to V$ be the restriction of $f$, so $f\circ j'=j\circ f'$. Restriction of modules to an open subscheme is the restriction along an open immersion of [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] it is isomorphic to the module pullback: $\mathcal M|_V\cong j^*\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N|_U\cong j'^*\mathcal N$, naturally. With the composition isomorphisms of pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] we get isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_U$-modules $$(f^*\mathcal G)|_U\cong j'^*f^*\mathcal G\cong(f\circ j')^*\mathcal G=(j\circ f')^*\mathcal G\cong f'^*j^*\mathcal G\cong f'^*(\mathcal G|_V),$$ the last one being $f'^*$ applied to the inverse of $\mathcal G|_V\cong j^*\mathcal G$. Call the composite $\theta:f'^*(\mathcal G|_V)\xrightarrow{\sim}(f^*\mathcal G)|_U$. (This is the reduction in the proof of Stacks 01B3, which uses Sheaves 0097 for the composition isomorphism.)

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01B6 (lemma-pullback-finite-type), proof, first sentence ('Arguing as in the proof of Lemma 01B3 we may assume G is globally generated'); Lemma 01B3 (lemma-pullback-locally-generated), proof, first paragraph, with Sheaves, Lemma 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules)

proof.text: *Step 2 (the pullback of the surjection is an epimorphism).* By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1) on the scheme $V$, the morphism $\varphi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_V$, being surjective as a map of sheaves, is an epimorphism of $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-epi-direct-sum](1) applied to $f':U\to V$, $f'^*\varphi:f'^*(\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n})\to f'^*(\mathcal G|_V)$ is an epimorphism of $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01B6, proof ('f^* ... is right exact, see Lemma 01AJ ... upon applying f^* we obtain the surjection'); Lemma 01AJ (lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback), part (2)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the pullback of $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}$ is $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-epi-direct-sum](2) for $f'$ and $\mathcal G_1=\dots=\mathcal G_n=\mathcal O_V$, the map $\sigma:\bigoplus_{i=1}^nf'^*\mathcal O_V\to f'^*(\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n})$ with components $f'^*(\iota_i)$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] for $f'$, $\epsilon_{f'}:f'^*\mathcal O_V\to\mathcal O_U$ is an isomorphism, so $\bigoplus_i\epsilon_{f'}^{-1}:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\bigoplus_if'^*\mathcal O_V$ is an isomorphism (a direct sum of isomorphisms). Hence $\tau=\sigma\circ\bigoplus_i\epsilon_{f'}^{-1}:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}f'^*(\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n})$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01B6, proof (the displayed surjection $\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathcal O_X\to f^*\mathcal G\to0$, which uses that $f^*$ commutes with direct sums, Lemma 01AJ(2), and $f^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X$, used there without reference)

proof.text: *Step 4 (conclusion).* The composite $\psi=\theta\circ f'^*\varphi\circ\tau:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to(f^*\mathcal G)|_U$ is an epimorphism of $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, being an epimorphism (Step 2) composed on both sides with isomorphisms (Steps 1 and 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting](1) on $U$, $\psi$ is surjective as a map of sheaves. Thus every $x\in X$ has the open neighbourhood $U=f^{-1}V$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow(f^*\mathcal G)|_U$, with the same $n$ as for $\mathcal G$ on $V$; that is, $f^*\mathcal G$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent].
